To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the gluon system is found to thermalize within the first 0.5-0.8 fm/c of the collision, (b) the thermalization time depends strongly on the initial gluon multiplicity and (c) the thermalization process is found to be strongly non-equilibrium in nature.

(1) partons thermalize in a time scale of about 0.1 fm/c, (2) parton energy loss in the parton cascade is consistent with the BDMPS-Z formalism, (3) parton cascades are useful to study parton energy loss and thermalization in ultrarelatistic heavy ion collisions, (4) the parton cascade approach is complementary to the Boltzmann transport approach, (5) the parton cascades is an efficient method
the parton thermalization is achieved in the parton cascade and the energy loss of high energy jets is well described.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of parton dynamics in the initial stage of heavy ion collisions at the LHC.
the study of partonic evolution in heavy ion collisions at RHIC and LHC energies.

the following questions: How does the initial gluon distribution evolve with time? Does the system reach local thermal equilibrium and if yes how long does it take? What is the role of the medium in jet quenching? How does the energy loss scale with the initial jet energy and how is the jet shape modified?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present parton cascade is capable of describing the main aspects of the thermalization of gluon fields, as well as the energy loss of jets.

the parton cascade model is a very useful tool for the description of the initial state of heavy ion collisions, the parton cascade dynamics, the evolution of the partonic matter and the final hadronization of this system.
the thermalization of the system in the initial stage is not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parton cascade is able to describe the parton dynamics from the early stage of the collisions, and the parton energy loss in this framework is comparable to the one obtained from other models.
we found that parton thermalization in a parton cascade can be described by the parton cascade itself, i.e. without introducing any phenomenological ansatz, such as the parton cascade model.
the parton cascading model, in its current form, does not describe the parton cascades in a satisfactory way, especially in the initial phase of the collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thermalization of gluon plasma is a fast process, which is completed within 1-2 fm/c, and that the energy loss of high-pT jets in the plasma is dominated by elastic collisions.

the parton cascade can describe the thermalization of gluon plasma and the energy loss of jets in a quantitative way, provided that the parton shower is initiated by hard scatterings and the parton interactions are treated in the leading-log approximation.

the thermalization process of partons in the early phase of the heavy ion collisions can be well captured by a simple phenomenological model, where partons are assumed to be in thermal equilibrium at a certain time, and the thermalization process can be viewed as a gradual increase of the temperature.
